meta.title: Q1 政策溫習卡
meta.note: Exam-style packs for English Q1 writing. Facts aligned to Q2 briefs / official PA & GIA sources — not City of Jade Data File fiction.

cards.prompt: Some argue that Government should sharply expand community care vouchers and day-care places while scaling back new subsidised residential care homes. Analyse the pros and cons, state a clear stance, and propose deliverable measures.
pros: Matches most elders’ preference to age in place and keep community ties.
Vouchers are more flexible and can stimulate home care, rehab and escort services faster than building homes.
Residential homes are land- and cost-intensive; community expansion can move sooner.
cons: Frail, dementia and unsupported elders still need residential places — vouchers alone are not enough.
Carer burden can be silently shifted to families if community wrap-around is weak.
Quality risk: large voucher volume without monitoring becomes ‘voucher in hand, service nowhere’.
cards.stance: Support ageing-in-place as the core, with residential care as a backstop — and strengthen carers.
measures: Raise community care vouchers to ~18,000 and residential care vouchers to ~8,000 by 2027-28, with new neighbourhood elderly / day centres.
Increase means-tested carer allowances and trial better-trained domestic helpers / carer training.
Scale gerontech (about HK$100m promotion envelope) to cut labour intensity of home care.

facts.text: Community care vouchers +2,000 → 18,000; residential care vouchers +1,000 → 8,000 (2027-28). 2026 PA Highlights.
Elderly Health Care Vouchers usable at designated GBA service points (latest gazette counts apply).

cards.prompt: Some argue that resources should prioritise primary care and community mental-health services, while deferring further expansion of large acute hospitals. Analyse the trade-offs, take a stance, and recommend measures.
pros: Prevention and early intervention can ease specialist / A&E load and are more cost-effective long term.
Community mental-health channels (DHCs, ICCMHs) reach youth and elders faster.
Extra family-medicine slots (including night clinics) support earlier chronic-disease management.
cons: Trauma, cancer and acute care still need hospital capacity; ageing raises inpatient demand.
Weak primary-to-hospital referral pathways send patients back to A&E.
Workforce scarcity means dual expansion can compete for the same clinicians.
cards.stance: Prioritise primary care + community mental health, without cutting acute hospital capability.
measures: Use District Health Centres as hubs for chronic care and mental-health triage, linked via eHealth; set KPIs on referral time and DNA rates.
Grow ambulatory / day surgery capacity on the hospital side to free beds.
Expand community psychiatric nurses and peer support — not beds alone — to shorten specialist waits.

facts.text: From next year: ~220,000 extra family-medicine outpatient slots/year (incl. ~10,000 night clinics); elderly health assessments more than doubled. 2026 PA Ch.VII.
eHealth registrations >6.5m (~87% of population). 2026 PA Ch.VII.
Mental-health package of 11 measures: three-tier school emergency mechanism, more ICCMHs, Joyous Heart pilot extension, etc. Same chapter.

cards.title_zh: 都市固體廢物收費與回收
cards.prompt: Some argue that Government should immediately restore and mandate city-wide municipal solid waste charging to hit waste-reduction targets. Analyse pros and cons, state a stance, and propose sequenced measures.
pros: Polluter-pays can shift behaviour and align with Waste Blueprint 2035 goals.
Can push source separation and lift recovery rates.
Long-run landfill relief frees land and environmental capacity.
cons: Livelihood pressure (esp. subdivided flats / low-income) and illegal dumping risk.
Hard launch before collection networks and enforcement are ready invites failure and backlash.
Charging is currently suspended — society needs a transition and education window.
cards.stance: Keep charging as a backstop; first deliver recovery infrastructure and habits, then restart in phases.
measures: Reach ‘one food-waste bin per estate’, ~3,000 smart recycling bins and ~2,500 smart food-waste bins; align messaging with Climate Action Plan 2050 / carbon-counting campaigns.
Pilot charging first at commercial premises, then residential, with recycling credits.
Couple with Transport Strategy Blueprint: public transport first, green mobility, ~5,000 EV fast chargers in five years.

facts.text: MSW recovery ~31% (2021) → ~34% (2024); food-waste recovery ~2.02 Mt (2024); daily MSW disposal ~10,326 tonnes (2025 publicity figure). info.gov.hk 2026-10-30.
MSW charging: suspended, not cancelled. Cross-check EEB.
Waste Blueprint 2035 mid-term: −40–45% per capita disposal; ~55% recovery.

cards.prompt: Some argue that, under intensifying extreme heat, Government should prioritise capital greening and shade in the hottest urban corridors over city-wide cash electricity subsidies or blanket midday outdoor work bans. Analyse the trade-offs, take a stance, and recommend a deliverable package.
pros: Corridor-focused shade / cool surfaces attacks the spatial driver of heat exposure and ambulance load.
Capital works can sit inside climate-adaptation envelopes with limited new recurrent spend if maintenance stays with existing departments.
Targeted means-tested relief plus overnight cooling places protect frail elders faster than landscaping alone.
cons: Greening alone does little for indoor heat in old private walk-ups tonight.
Open-ended electricity top-ups create recurrent fiscal pressure.
Hard midday stoppages without flexibility hit SME logistics and construction hard and face weak compliance.
cards.stance: Pilot cool-corridor capital + capped vulnerable relief first; soft outdoor-work guidance before city-wide mandates.
measures: Phase 1: shade, trees, cool pavement and selected PRH/elderly common-area upgrades in the worst corridors; overnight cooling centres on Very Hot Weather Warning nights.
Time-limited, means-tested summer electricity top-up only for low-income elderly inside those corridors, with a hard spend cap and two-summer review.
Industry rest-break / shaded-rest guidance now; revisit mandatory cool-roof / façade rules for existing SME stock only after pilots and a funded transition path.

facts.text: Climate Action Plan 2050: cut total carbon emissions by half from 2005 before 2035; carbon neutrality before 2050; urban forestry cited to ease heat-island effects.
Building electricity goals: commercial −30–40% and residential −20–30% from 2015 by 2050 (half by 2035). ACE Paper 11/2026.
Government maintains about one million trees under TRAM / urban forestry programmes (DEVB greening).

cards.prompt: With cross-boundary travel becoming routine (incl. Northern Metropolis planning), some argue peak-crowd border response (e.g. Halloween flows) should be institutionalised with clear short-term lead departments and measurable ‘smoothness’ KPIs, rather than one-off mobilisation. Analyse, take a stance, and propose measures.
pros: Clear lead and KPIs cut ‘who decides’ delays at peak and speed redeployment.
Standing SOPs prepare for denser daily NM-related flows, not just festival spikes.
Publishing wait-time / diversion / incident metrics builds trust and after-action accountability.
cons: Over-rigid SOPs can strip frontline flexibility for unusual incidents.
Multi-bureau clearance chains (SB / TLB etc.) can slow decisions if every step escalates.
KPIs that only reward ‘speed’ may trade off inspection quality and safety.
cards.stance: Institutionalise peak response with clear lead + smoothness KPIs, while keeping on-site flexibility.
measures: Standing peak SOP: triggers, command chain, on-site authority; CS-level cross-bureau steering; day-to-day execution by SB / TLB by function.
Publish smoothness KPIs: wait-time percentiles, public-transport diversion punctuality/load, incident response times; 72-hour post-peak brief.
Put foreseeable peaks on an annual drill calendar; extend pilots to other land crossings and link to NM passenger forecasts.

facts.text: Huanggang Port activated a cross-department peak response for Halloween flows (window ~30 Oct–1 Nov).
Steering at Chief Secretary level; Security Bureau and Transport and Logistics Bureau in the execution split.
Policy angle: border resilience should plug into Northern Metropolis / routine cross-boundary travel, not one-off mobilisation only.

cards.prompt: Some argue that without scene validation, outcome KPIs and talent-retention metrics, New Industrialisation Funding Scheme / Accelerator support will stay ‘policy without delivery’. Should funding be tightly bound to delivery checks? Analyse, take a stance, and recommend measures.
pros: Binding grants to validation and KPIs cuts ‘approve-and-forget’ and raises public-money accountability.
Accelerator + funding optimisation can move advanced manufacturing / prototypes into real scenes faster.
Retention metrics address the ‘projects without people’ risk in I&T.
cons: Over-tight checks slow approvals; SMEs may struggle with compliance costs.
Scene validation needs cross-bureau coordination — firms may apply elsewhere short term.
Talent stay is driven by housing/tax/family factors a single grant cannot fully carry.
cards.stance: Bind funding to delivery checks, but phase them and keep them operable — with an SME-light track.
measures: Phase: require minimum scene validation first in selected use-cases (e.g. advanced manufacturing / medical-device prototypes), then widen.
Verifiable KPIs: milestone hit-rate, local R&D/jobs, key talent retained in HK; miss → adjust later tranches.
ITIB + scheme administrators publish a one-page scorecard and annual outcomes report; simplify the SME channel.

facts.text: New Industrialisation Funding Scheme (from Sep 2024) is a main current tool (cite scheme name + timing in the exam).
New Industrialisation Acceleration Scheme runs alongside, stressing faster industry landing.
Public discussion has cited funding bands around ~HK$2.8m / HK$15m — always check the latest official ceiling; do not treat one figure as the only cap.

cards.title_zh: 河套東連收地與北都落地
cards.prompt: Some argue that Northern Metropolis ‘ready sites’ depend on faster resumption for supporting roads such as the Hetao East Link, cross-bureau coordination, and measurable compensation outcomes — not blueprint announcements alone. Analyse, take a stance, and propose measures.
pros: Aligning resumption to road / infrastructure nodes shortens the ‘planned but not ready’ gap for I&T and industry land.
Clear cross-bureau lead cuts mutual waiting and makes construction / handover dates more predictable.
Transparent compensation and relocation metrics lower protest/litigation risk and lift delivery confidence.
cons: Rushing resumption without synced compensation/relocation can inflame communities and delay works.
One-size timelines ignore plot-level legal and engineering complexity and raise cost.
Making compensation satisfaction the only KPI can prolong negotiation and miss ready-site targets.
cards.stance: Align resumption to infrastructure nodes + cross-bureau coordination + measurable compensation — no blueprint-only storytelling.
measures: Publish phased resumption and ready-site handover targets keyed to nodes (e.g. Hetao East Link), with named lead departments.
Standing Lands / Transport / bureau coordination with escalation triggers; quarterly public progress briefs.
Compensation KPIs: agreement rate, relocation-on-time, business transition completion; miss → fix process, not just publicity.

facts.text: Hetao East Link: resume 112 private lots (~5.7 ha); plus ~113 m² government land occupied by graves/urns; reverts to Government 3 months after notice (2027-01-30). info.gov.hk 2026-10-29.
Core tension: whether resumption keeps pace with ready-site supply, and whether cross-bureau coordination cuts mutual waiting.
Effectiveness lens: published, verifiable compensation/relocation — not plans alone.

cards.title_zh: 中小企數碼轉型與資安
cards.prompt: Some argue that SME digital subsidies should shift from approval volume to sustained tool use and basic cybersecurity outcomes (MFA, backups, phishing resilience), with a ring-fenced micro-firm track. Analyse pros and cons, take a stance, and recommend measures.
pros: Outcome KPIs (still-in-use, cyber hygiene) curb ‘grant consultants + shelfware’.
Matching support for AI and cybersecurity under DTSPP matches real SME risk after rushed e-commerce setup.
A micro-firm track offsets skew toward larger SMEs that can already write better applications.
cons: Heavy outcome audits raise admin burden and may deter the weakest firms.
Pure vouchers can race to the bottom on insecure cheap software.
Cyber capability gaps mean training must be bundled or take-up stays cosmetic.
cards.stance: Keep matching grants, but pay later tranches on verified use + basic cyber; ring-fence micro firms.
measures: Enhance DTSPP matching subsidies for AI and cybersecurity solutions; publish still-in-use and MFA/backup KPIs at 6–12 months.
Raise Easy BUD ceiling use and AI-targeted BUD support; keep Digital DIY Portal advisory + cyber risk checks via HKPC.
Ring-fence a micro-firm (<10 staff) quota with pre-approved vendor list and mandatory short cyber hygiene module before final payment.

facts.text: 2026 PA: 10 SME support measures — incl. Easy BUD ceiling raised to HK$150,000 (Jun) and more AI-targeted BUD support.
DTSPP to be enhanced with matching subsidies for more SMEs adopting AI and cybersecurity solutions. 2026 PA Ch.III.
BUD Fund: cumulative ceiling HK$7m per enterprise; general application ceiling HK$800,000; Easy BUD HK$150,000 (30 working-day pledge).

quick_ref.stance_one_liner: Ageing-in-place core; residential as backstop + carers.
Primary + community mental health first; keep acute capacity.
Charging as backstop; infrastructure & habits first.
Cool-corridor capital + capped relief before mandates.
Institutionalise peaks + KPIs; keep on-site flexibility.
Bind funding to delivery KPIs; phase + SME-light track.
Pay on verified use + cyber; ring-fence micros.
